relations.subject: search:full-text-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (hasInternalComponent)
relations.evidence: A basic Search index is a list of all of the unique terms that appear in the documents stored in your cluster. For each term, the Search index also contains a list of the documents where that term appears. This list is called an inverted index.

relations.subject: search:full-text-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (hasInternalComponent)
relations.evidence: The inverted index, term dictionary, or the vector index are stored in [Search Index Segments](#segments), which are sent to the disk write queue and saved to disk through [synchronization with the Data Service](#sync).

relations.subject: search:full-text-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (hasInternalComponent)

notable_absence.finding: This page never states how many index-persister or index-merger routines run per node/partition, nor whether they are configurable - it describes their existence and division of labor but not their cardinality or tunability, unlike the surrounding partition/replica material elsewhere in this batch (fts:index-partitioning, fts:index-replicas) which is explicit about counts.

cross_component_finding: This page (search/search-index-architecture.md) independently restates three facts already established from a completely different part of the tree, server/8.0/learn/services-and-indexes/services/search-service.json: that the Search Service uses a scatter-gather execution model, that a per-request coordinator node is assumed ad hoc, and that the Search Service streams data via DCP from the Data Service. All three are confirmed consistently across the two independent sources rather than contradicted, and this page adds the specific detail (gRPC as the scatter transport) that the services/search-service.json source did not mention at all - a genuine addition rather than mere repetition.
